title: Inference, profiling and measured performance
outcome: Explain which work a timing includes, inspect type inference and measure a small kernel without turning machine-dependent timing into a correctness assertion.

exercises.title: Trace the accumulator
exercises.task: Trace total after each element of [1.0,2.0,3.0].
exercises.answer: The accumulator is Float64 throughout; the final value is 14.

exercises.title: Preserve precision
exercises.hint: Inspect typeof as well as value.
exercises.answer: zero(T) and floating multiplication preserve the specified small-case element arithmetic.

exercises.title: Change workload size
exercises.expected: Both return four times their length; observed time may vary.
exercises.hint: Do not assert which individual call is faster.
exercises.answer: A larger workload changes the experiment. Multiple observations are needed to compare scaling.

exercises.title: Diagnose invalid science
exercises.task: Pass [NaN] and explain why inference still succeeds.
exercises.hint: A known type is not a finite value.
exercises.answer: Inference concerns types. Scientific input validation is a separate contract.

exercises.title: Design a benchmark record
exercises.task: List the fields needed to reproduce a timing claim.
exercises.expected: Include input, versions, threads, cold/warm boundary and repetitions.
exercises.hint: Keep correctness results with the timings.
exercises.answer: A benchmark record identifies environment and work; a number without these cannot support a transferable claim.

exercises.title: Transfer to a data pipeline
exercises.task: Identify which parsing, fitting and plotting boundaries you would measure.
exercises.answer: Phase measurements explain bottlenecks while end-to-end time captures the actual user experience.
